candidate.answerReason: Reflection across the drawn diagonal pairs each shaded piece with an unshaded piece of equal area. These pairs fill the square, so the shaded and unshaded totals are equal.

methods.label: Pair shaded and unshaded pieces
methods.explanation:
The drawn diagonal suggests folding the square to compare its pieces without calculating their individual areas.

[Figure 1](figures/1990_AMC_8_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

Reflect across the diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. The small shaded triangle matches the small unshaded triangle. The middle shaded piece matches the middle unshaded piece, and the top shaded piece matches the unshaded piece on the right.

Reflection preserves area, so each pair contains equal shaded and unshaded areas. Since the three pairs fill the square, half of the square is shaded. The fraction is \(\boxed{\tfrac12}\), choice \(\text{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Folding, equal-area pairing, and the meaning of one half are accessible elementary spatial reasoning.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is the area fraction of a composite shaded region. The written method combines areas through three reflected pairs, so elementary line symmetry is method-local knowledge. Area meaning and the interpretation of one half support the conclusion. No equal-third divisions or individual dimensions are needed, and the more advanced perpendicular-bisector properties of reflection are not used. These annotations do not establish mastery.

review.mathematicalCheck: In the actual figure, reflection across the bottom-left to top-right diagonal exchanges each shaded region with its unshaded partner. These three disjoint pairs fill the square, so shaded and unshaded areas are equal and the shaded fraction is 1/2.
review.levelCheck: Folding and equal-area pairing are appropriate elementary spatial reasoning.
review.annotationCheck: Composite area, elementary line symmetry, area meaning, and unit fractions accurately describe the written reasoning. No stronger reflection properties are required.
